baselinePanel.contract: Fixed prompt set for month-over-month AI answer visibility. Prompts are append-only; rewording an existing id invalidates the trend.

amendments.change: Appended high-signal as the seventh tracked surface (6 prompts, 40 -> 46).
amendments.why: High Signal was promoted to a priority surface. The panel had not been executed yet when this was appended (SAR-11 is blocked on fixture-only execution), so no month-over-month trend existed to invalidate. Adding the surface now costs nothing; adding it after the first real run would have cost a baseline.

amendments.change: Froze the five-engine set (chatgpt, claude, perplexity, gemini, copilot) and raised runBudget.maxCalls on the seven panel surfaces to expandedPrompts x 5.
amendments.why: Route A (operator-captured observations) was selected. maxCalls was sized for exactly one provider per surface, so prepareProviderObservationRuns would have thrown 'requires N calls, exceeding maxCalls' on all seven surfaces the moment a five-engine capture was ingested. No live call is made on this path; the guard bounds ingest volume, not spend.

amendments.change: Appended manual-claude-websearch as a sixth engine column and raised runBudget.maxCalls on the seven panel surfaces to expandedPrompts x 6.
amendments.why: Baseline run 1 was executed and written to the ledger under the column id manual-claude-websearch, which the five-engine freeze did not declare. That column is agent-session grounded retrieval, not the claude.ai web UI, so relabelling it 'claude' would silently mix two retrieval backends into one trend line. Declaring it as its own column is the honest reconciliation; the budget follows the engine count so a full six-column sweep does not throw.

engines.label: Claude (agent session, grounded web search)
engines.note: Distinct from the 'claude' column: a different retrieval backend reached without a browser session, so it carries no account personalization. This is the column baseline run 1 was captured on.

baselinePanel.engineContract: Engines are frozen alongside the prompts. Month-over-month AI-answer visibility is only comparable if the same prompt set runs against the same engine set. Adding or dropping an engine is an amendment, and the trend restarts for the affected engine only. A rate is only comparable to another rate captured on the same engine column; never average across columns or read a single-column rate as a panel-wide number.

baselineRuns.note: First real execution of the frozen panel. 10.8% is the manual-claude-websearch column only, not a six-engine panel figure. The five operator-web-ui columns are uncaptured; their trend starts at their own first run.
